rendered:
Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity falls below 80%[1] of its rated capacity.

At that point the end-of-life EV batteries can be reused/repurposed, recycled, or disposed of in landfills. The review notes that landfill disposal would cause serious environmental issues. The repurposing route gives the batteries a second life in applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage.

The review says that the batteries which are reused will still eventually need to be recycled: regardless of whether batteries are reused, they will eventually need to be recycled.[2][3][4][5]
